new.s: Which provision of the Constitution allows a person who is not a Member of Parliament to be appointed a Union Minister for a limited period?
new.x: Article 75(5) lets a non-member be a Minister, but he ceases to be one if he does not become an MP within six consecutive months.
new.angle: U0301 #3/#10 PYQ ya5632fe30a5 non-member minister -> Article clause

new.s: P.V. Narasimha Rao became Prime Minister in 1991 without being a Member of Parliament. Within what period did he have to become a member of either House?
new.x: Under Article 75(5) a non-member PM or Minister must become an MP within six consecutive months.
new.angle: U0301 #10/#11 non-member PM -> maximum period

new.s: What did the 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003 provide?
o: The Council of Ministers, including the PM, shall not exceed 15% of the total strength of the Lok Sabha
The President may return ministerial advice once for reconsideration
Reservation of one-third seats for women in the Lok Sabha
new.x: The 91st Amendment (2003) inserted Article 75(1A) capping the Union ministry at 15% of the Lok Sabha; the 97th dealt with co-operatives.
new.angle: U0301 #2/#9 size cap -> amendment (APPSC G2 2025)

new.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003:
1. The 15% limit on the Union Council of Ministers includes the Prime Minister.
2. In a State, the number of Ministers, including the Chief Minister, shall not be less than 12.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Article 75(1A) counts the PM within the 15% cap, and Article 164(1A) sets a minimum of 12 Ministers in a State.
new.angle: U0301 #9 percentage rule; PYQ y9c73f3f830e State minimum 12

new.s: Which Article of the Constitution fixes the 15% limit and the minimum of 12 on the size of a State Council of Ministers?

new.angle: U0301 PYQ y9c73f3f830e State ministry size -> Article
